# DPP criteria catalogue

Readable overview of all criteria in this folder. Each criterion is defined in one YAML file; this page is generated from those files, so the YAML file is the reference if the two ever differ. The file format is described in [CRITERIA-FORMAT.md](../CRITERIA-FORMAT.md).

Statements paraphrase their sources; they are not quotations of the standards. Only `active` criteria count in published results; `proposed` criteria are under review. Results state how many automated checks passed on a given day. They are not a certification and do not establish a presumption of conformity.

## Overview

| | active | proposed | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Published passport (dpplint) | 6 | 16 | 22 |
| DPP service (dpp-validator) | 14 | 2 | 16 |
| Economic operator (self-declared) | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| **All criteria** | 20 | 19 | 39 |

How to read the entries:

- **Level**: MUST, SHOULD or MAY as in RFC 2119.
- **Checked on**: *published passport* means the passport fetched via its product identifier (checked by [dpplint](https://github.com/OwnYourData/dpplint)); *DPP service* means the API of a listed service (checked daily by [dpp-validator](https://github.com/OwnYourData/dpp-validator)); *economic operator* means an obligation the operator declares.
- **Method**: *automated* checks run from the public internet with test data only; *with test credentials* also needs a token from the operator; *self-declared* means the operator states it and links evidence.
- **Results**: passed, failed, warning (passed with a remark) or skipped (condition not met or data not available). Only passed and failed count in "N of M".
- **Placeholders** in requests: `{base}` API base of the service, `{dppId}` and `{productId}` its test passport ID and product identifier, `{elementIdPath}` a JSONPath into the test passport, `{randomId}` an ID no service has issued, `{now}` the run time in UTC.

## Scope and configuration

### DPP-CFG-005

**Granularity matches the product identifier**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The granularity of a DPP MUST match the level (model, batch or item) that its unique product identifier identifies.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 9(2)(d) (regulation)
- EN 18223:2026, 4.1.2.2 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18219:2026, 4.4.2 (1), 5.2.2.1 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** Checked in the SOyA structure DigitalProductPassport for identifiers in GS1 Digital Link form (ID scheme 1, EN 18219 5.2.2.1): /21/ means item, /10/ batch, otherwise model. Other schemes do not encode the level and are not rated. The allowed values are checked by DPP-DAT-015.

## Identification

### DPP-ID-001

**Product identifier resolves to its passport**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 2

> A DPP MUST be connected to a persistent unique product identifier that resolves to exactly this passport.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 10(1)(a) (regulation)
- EN 18219:2026, 4.5.2 (1) (harmonised standard)
- EN 18220:2026, 5.2.1 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The product identifier is opened like a phone scanning the data carrier (plain HTTPS GET with `Accept: application/json`). Expected: a single passport object whose `uniqueProductIdentifier` equals the identifier.

**Notes** Only the digital half is testable: the identifier resolves to one passport object (not a list) whose uniqueProductIdentifier equals the input. Whether the physical data carrier is on the product is out of scope. The request states Accept application/json, so that the result does not depend on which format the service returns without a stated preference (assessed by DPP-DAT-016).

Catalogue rows: DPP-ID-001, DPP-CAR-004 · Source: [id/DPP-ID-001.yaml](id/DPP-ID-001.yaml)

### DPP-ID-002

**Product identifier stays resolvable over time**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The unique product identifier MUST keep resolving to its passport for as long as the passport has to be available.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 10(1)(a) (regulation)
- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 9(2)(i) (regulation)
- EN 18219:2026, 4.2.2 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18221:2026, 4.1 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The product identifier is opened like a phone scanning the data carrier (plain HTTPS GET). Expected: a single passport object whose `uniqueProductIdentifier` equals the identifier.

Rated only from the validator's daily runs: fails after 3 consecutive days without success.

**Notes** Rated only by the validator from its daily runs against the test data of a listed service; single failures appear in the history. A single linter run does not rate this criterion (see DPP-ID-001).

### DPP-ID-009

**Economic operator identifier follows an EN 18219 scheme**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> Where an economic operator identifier is required, it MUST follow one of the ID schemes for economic operators in EN 18219.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Annex III (g), (h), (k) (regulation)
- EN 18219:2026, 6.1 (harmonised standard)

**Applies only if** the passport meets: `$.economicOperatorId` exists (otherwise skipped).

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** Checked in the SOyA structure DigitalProductPassport by syntax: ISO/IEC 6523 (ICD prefix), GS1 GLN or Digital Link (ISO/IEC 15418), DID or DOI. Whether the identifier is present is checked by DPP-ROL-016; DID-specific requirements by DPP-ID-016. The EU DPP registry accepts only NTR, LEI, VAT and eID identifiers for economic operators.

### DPP-ID-013

**Passport readable without registration or credentials**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 1

> Public DPP information MUST be retrievable through the product identifier without registration, DPP-specific software or user credentials.

**Basis**

- EN 18219:2026, 4.6.2 (2), (3) (harmonised standard)
- EN 18220:2026, 5.3.4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The product identifier is opened like a phone scanning the data carrier (plain HTTPS GET). Expected: status 200.

**Product identifier is a URL or convertible to one**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The unique product identifier MUST be a URL or be convertible into a URL by a specified method.

**Basis**

- EN 18219:2026, 4.3.2 (2) (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** Checked in the SOyA structure DigitalProductPassport by syntax: an HTTP(S) URL, a DID (resolved by DID Resolution), an EPC URN (converted per the GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard) or an ISO/IEC 15434 message (converted per ISO/IEC 18975).

### DPP-ID-016

**DID identifiers follow DID Core, DID Resolution and VC 2.0**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 1

> Where the economic operator or facility identifier is a DID, it MUST conform to DID Core 1.0 and be resolvable with DID Resolution, and credentials associated with it MUST follow the VC Data Model 2.0.

**Basis**

- EN 18219:2026, 6.4.2 a)–c) (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The DIDs found at `$.economicOperatorId` and `$.facilityId` are resolved and checked against DID Core and DID Resolution; values that are not DIDs are skipped. Associated credentials are checked against the VC Data Model 2.0.

**Notes** Values that are not DIDs are skipped. Resolution uses didlint. Associated credentials are not required; if there are none, a warning is given. No issuer is prescribed (EN 18219 6.4.3 lists registries only as an option).

Source: [id/DPP-ID-016.yaml](id/DPP-ID-016.yaml)

## Data carrier

### DPP-CAR-002

**Product identifier follows an EN 18219 product scheme**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The unique product identifier MUST follow one of the product ID schemes of EN 18219.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 10(1)(c) (regulation)
- EN 18219:2026, 4.3.2, Clause 5 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18220:2026, 5.2.2 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** Checked in the SOyA structure DigitalProductPassport by syntax: HTTPS URL (schemes 1, 2 and 5), DID (scheme 3) or RFID/2D encoding (scheme 4). Only the identifier is checked; conformity of the physical data carrier (EN 18220) cannot be observed.

**Passport contains the product-specific mandatory data**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> A DPP MUST contain all data elements that the applicable product-specific rules make mandatory.

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 9(1) (regulation)

## Data model and semantics

### DPP-DAT-003

**Passport is delivered as structured JSON**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 2

> DPP data MUST be machine-readable and structured, delivered as a JSON object based on open standards.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 10(1)(d) (regulation)
- EN 18216:2026, 5 a) (harmonised standard)
- EN 18223:2026, 5.2.4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The product identifier is opened like a phone scanning the data carrier (plain HTTPS GET with `Accept: application/json`). Expected: status 200; content type `application/json`.

**Notes** The response has to parse as a single JSON object. Attribute names are checked by DPP-DAT-014. The request states Accept application/json: the criterion asks whether the passport is available as JSON, not which format a client without a stated preference receives; that is assessed by DPP-DAT-016.

### DPP-DAT-006

**Passport follows the Commission's semantic data models**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> DPP data MUST be structured according to the common data models and semantic definitions of the semantic repository.

**Basis**

- [Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 (DPP registry)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1778/oj), Art. 11(3); Art. 2(12) (regulation)
- EN 18223:2026, 4.3 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against shapes from the European Commission's semantic repository. If no shapes are found, the result is skipped.

**Notes** Data elements link to their definitions through dictionaryReference. Includes value ranges, units, formats and vocabularies defined there. No semantic catalogue is published yet, so the result is skipped until one exists.

### DPP-DAT-011

**Related resources are typed and reachable**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> Links from a DPP to other passports or resources MUST carry a content type and a resolvable URL.

**Basis**

- [Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 (DPP registry)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1778/oj), Art. 12(1)(a) (regulation)
- EN 18223:2026, 4.1.2.7 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18221:2026, 4.1, 4.4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Every `RelatedResource` element of the passport must have `contentType` and `url`, and its URL must answer. A URL that does not answer gives a warning.

**Notes** A URL that does not answer is reported as a warning, so that outages of third-party sites do not fail the passport. Without RelatedResource elements the result is skipped.

### DPP-DAT-014

**Passport header uses the EN 18223 attributes**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> A DPP MUST carry the attributes of the DigitalProductPassport class under their published names, including all mandatory ones (digitalProductPassportId, uniqueProductIdentifier, granularity, dppSchemaVersion, dppStatus, lastUpdated, economicOperatorId).

**Basis**

- EN 18223:2026, 4.1.2.1, Table 1; 5.2.2 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** facilityId is optional (0..1), contentSpecificationIds may repeat (0..\*). lastUpdated is an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. dppStatus is a free string; values outside the examples active, inactive, archived, invalid give a warning, independent of capitalisation. dppSchemaVersion and contentSpecificationIds are strings and are not resolved. A passport ID that is not a URI gives a warning. Draft-era names (ProductID, DPPStatus, …) fail because the published attribute is missing.

> The attribute granularity MUST take one of the values model, batch or item.

### DPP-DAT-016

**Passport is available as HTML**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 3

> A DPP MUST also be provided as HTML through HTTP content negotiation.

**Basis**

- EN 18216:2026, 5 a), 5 d) (harmonised standard)
- [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-vary), 12.5.5 (standard)
- [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-accept), 12.5.1 (standard)

**How it is checked** The product identifier is opened like a phone scanning the data carrier (plain HTTPS GET with `Accept: text/html`). Expected: status 200; content type `text/html`; header `Vary` lists `Accept` (warning only).

- Further request with `Accept: */*`: expect status 200; content type `application/json` (warning only).
- Further request with `Accept: application/json, text/html;q=0.1`: expect status 200; content type `application/json` (warning only).

**Notes** Only the HTML request decides pass or fail. Three further checks give at most a warning. (1) The HTML response lists Accept in its Vary header (RFC 9110 12.5.5), so that caches do not hand the HTML variant to JSON clients or the other way round; "Vary: \*" does not count. (2) A request with Accept \*/\* still returns application/json: JSON is the required format of EN 18216 Clause 5 and HTML is added only through content negotiation, so a client that states no preference keeps receiving JSON. (3) A request that prefers JSON and accepts HTML only with a low quality value (RFC 9110 12.5.1) returns application/json, so that the service weighs quality values instead of only looking for media types in the header. The accessibility requirements of the same clause (EN 301 549) are not checked automatically.

Source: [dat/DPP-DAT-016.yaml](dat/DPP-DAT-016.yaml)

## APIs and data exchange

### DPP-API-007

**Errors use the EN 18222 status codes**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 2

> A DPP service MUST answer faulty requests with the status codes of EN 18222 and MUST NOT answer them with a server error.

**Basis**

- EN 18222:2026, 7.2, Table 15 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `POST /dppsByProductIds`, without credentials, header `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{not json` → expect status 400
2. `POST /dppsByProductIds`, without credentials, header `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{"productId": 42}` → expect status 400

**Notes** Checks malformed requests to ReadDPPIdsByProductIds. The answer to an unknown passport ID (404) is checked by DPP-API-022, so that it is also assessed in a read-only run.

Catalogue rows: DPP-API-007 · Source: [api/DPP-API-007.yaml](api/DPP-API-007.yaml)

### DPP-API-013

**Lifecycle API provides ReadDPPById**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> The DPP lifecycle API MUST provide the method ReadDPPById without requiring credentials for public data.

**Basis**

- EN 18222:2026, 4.1, 4.2, 8.2 (harmonised standard)

- EN 18219:2026, 4.6.2 (3) (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `GET /dpps/{dppId}`, without credentials → expect status 200; content type `application/json`; `$.digitalProductPassportId` equals `{dppId}`

**Lifecycle API provides ReadDPPIdsByProductIds**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> The DPP lifecycle API MUST provide the method ReadDPPIdsByProductIds, so that passports can be found by product identifier.

- EN 18222:2026, 4.1, 4.5, 8.2 (harmonised standard)
- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 10(1)(d) (regulation)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `POST /dppsByProductIds`, without credentials, header `Content-Type: application/json`, body `["{productId}"]` → expect status 200; content type `application/json`; `$..[?@ == '{dppId}']` exists; status 400 → warning

**Notes** The standard does not fix the JSON form of the request body; the check sends an array of product identifiers. If a service rejects that form with 400, a warning is given instead of a failure. The ID is accepted in a bare array or in a wrapping object.

### DPP-API-021

**elementIdPath uses RFC 9535 JSONPath**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 2

> The value of elementIdPath in the fine-granular API MUST follow RFC 9535 (JSONPath).

**Basis**

- EN 18222:2026, 7.2, 8.1, 8.4, Tables 15 and 18 (harmonised standard)

**Applies only if** the service declares the feature `fine-granular-api`.

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `GET /dpps/{dppId}/elements/{elementIdPath}`, without credentials → expect status 200; content type `application/json`
2. `GET /dpps/{dppId}/elements/%24%5B`, without credentials → expect status 400

**Notes** The fine-granular API itself is optional (EN 18222 6.1); the criterion applies only to services that declare it. The test data of the service names a JSONPath to a known data element. Step 1 requests it without the representation query flag, so the service answers in the default compressed representation (EN 18222 8.1, EN 18223 5.2), where the element may be a bare value, array or object without an elementId; step 1 therefore checks only status and content type. Step 2 sends the syntactically invalid expression "$\[". EN 18222 Table 15 maps a malformed request to ClientErrorBadRequest (400); 404 is not accepted, since a service that does not evaluate JSONPath at all would also answer 404.

Source: [api/DPP-API-021.yaml](api/DPP-API-021.yaml)

### DPP-API-022

**Unknown passport ID is answered with 404**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> A DPP service MUST answer a request for a passport ID it does not hold with the status code ClientErrorResourceNotFound (404) of EN 18222.

**Basis**

- EN 18222:2026, 7.2, Table 15 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `GET /dpps/{randomId}`, without credentials → expect status 404; `$.message` exists (warning only)

**Notes** Taken over from version 1 of DPP-API-007, so that it is also assessed in a read-only run. Table 15 lists a result object for 404; a missing one gives a warning. 200 or 204 with an empty body is not accepted: the client could not tell an unknown passport from an empty answer.

### DPP-API-023

**API honours the representation query flag**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The DPP API MUST return the compressed representation when the representation query flag is absent or set to compressed, and the full representation when it is set to full.

**Basis**

- EN 18222:2026, 8.1 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18223:2026, 5.2.2, Annex A (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `GET /dpps/{dppId}`, without credentials → expect status 200; content type `application/json`; `$.digitalProductPassportId` equals `{dppId}`; `$.elements` does not exist
2. `GET /dpps/{dppId}?representation=compressed`, without credentials → expect status 200; content type `application/json`; `$.elements` does not exist
3. `GET /dpps/{dppId}?representation=full`, without credentials → expect status 200; content type `application/json`; `$.elements[0].elementId` exists
4. `GET /dpps/{dppId}?representation=dpp-validator-unknown`, without credentials → expect status 400 (a failure of this step gives only a warning)

**Notes** In the compressed representation (EN 18223 5.2.2) data elements are keyed by their elementId and the metadata is left out, so the passport has no elements array; the full representation (Annex A) lists them under elements with elementId and objectType. The check relies on that difference and assumes that no data element of the test passport has the elementId "elements". EN 18222 8.1 defines only the two values; another value is a malformed request (Table 15, 400), which gives at most a warning.

Source: [api/DPP-API-023.yaml](api/DPP-API-023.yaml)

**HTTPS with a valid certificate**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> Standardised DPP access MUST use HTTPS with a valid certificate; plain HTTP MUST be redirected to HTTPS or refused.

**Basis**

- EN 18216:2026, 4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** TLS and HTTP properties of the host of the API base:

- the certificate chain and host name verify against the common public CA set
- plain HTTP on port 80 serves nothing: it redirects to `https://`, refuses the connection or answers with an error status

**TLS 1.2 or higher, older versions refused**

**Basis**

- EN 18216:2026, 4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** TLS and HTTP properties of the host of the API base:

- at least TLS 1.2 is negotiated
- handshakes offering only SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 are refused
- TLS 1.3 is offered (otherwise a warning)

**Notes** TLS 1.3 is recommended; its absence gives a warning.

### DPP-DEX-005

**HTTP/2 is supported**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> DPP communication MUST support HTTP/2.

**Basis**

- EN 18216:2026, 4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** TLS and HTTP properties of the host of the API base:

### DPP-DEX-006

**HTTP versions below HTTP/2 are not used**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 1

> DPP communication MUST NOT use HTTP versions older than HTTP/2.

**Basis**

- EN 18216:2026, 4 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** TLS and HTTP properties of the host of the API base:

- requests forced to HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1 get no successful (2xx/3xx) answer

**Notes** Checked on the HTTPS port of the API base only; port 80 (redirect to HTTPS, ACME HTTP-01) is not tested and stays covered by DPP-DEX-002. A request forced to HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1 over TLS counts as rejected if it gets no successful response: aborted connection or TLS handshake, or a status of 400 or higher. A 2xx or 3xx answer at either version fails the criterion. Recommended answer: refuse HTTP/1.x already in the TLS handshake (ALPN offers only h2), or answer 400 (ClientErrorBadRequest) with the result object of EN 18222. 505 HTTP Version Not Supported is not recommended, since it is not among the status codes that EN 18222:2026 Table 15 allows. See the tls check type in CRITERIA-FORMAT.md.

Source: [dex/DPP-DEX-006.yaml](dex/DPP-DEX-006.yaml)

## Security, integrity and privacy

### DPP-SEC-001

**Passport cannot be changed without authorisation**

**MUST** · checked on: DPP service · automated · status: active · version 2

> A DPP service MUST reject attempts to create or change passports without valid authorisation.

**Basis**

- EN 18221:2026, 4.1 (harmonised standard)
- EN 18222:2026, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, Table 15 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** Requests to the API base of the service, in this order:

1. `GET /dpps/{dppId}`, without credentials → expect status 200
2. `PATCH /dpps/{dppId}`, without credentials, header `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{}` → expect status 400, 401, 403, 404, 405 or 501
3. `POST /dpps`, without credentials, header `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{}` → expect status 400, 401, 403, 404, 405 or 501
4. `GET /dpps/{dppId}`, without credentials → expect status 200; body identical to step 1

**Notes** The PATCH body changes nothing, so a wrongly accepted request leaves the test passport intact. No DELETE is sent against the test passport. Steps 2 and 3 accept every client error of EN 18222 Table 15 that refuses the request without creating or changing anything (400, 401, 403, 404, 405) and 501, because a service without a write API may reject the empty body or the route before any authorisation check. Whether the passport stayed unchanged is decided by step 4.

Catalogue rows: DPP-SEC-001, DPP-API-005 · Source: [sec/DPP-SEC-001.yaml](sec/DPP-SEC-001.yaml)

### DPP-SEC-002

**Integrity of the passport version is verifiable**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: active · version 2

> The integrity of a DPP version MUST be verifiable.

**Basis**

- [Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 (DPP registry)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2026/1778/oj), Art. 2 (hash of the version); Art. 8(9) (regulation)
- EN 18221:2026, 4.1, 4.2 (harmonised standard)
- prEN 18246:2025, 4.7 (draft standard)

**How it is checked** The integrity proofs of the passport are verified (formats: `vc-data-integrity`, `vc-jose-cose` and `did-oyd-log`). Without a proof the result is skipped.

**Notes** EN 18221:2026 requires DPP service providers to ensure the integrity and authenticity of stored passports and of archived versions, following EN 18246; prEN 18246:2025 4.7 asks that a DPP be verifiable in integrity and authenticity, free of charge for the verifier. Every proof found is verified with the key it names (verificationMethod, JWS kid) or, for did-oyd-log, against the payloadHash in the DID document of the passport identifier; who holds the key is assessed in DPP-SEC-013. Only the current version is checked. Without a proof the result is skipped. The version hash under Art. 8(9) of the Implementing Regulation is held by the EU DPP registry, which has no public API.

Catalogue rows: DPP-SEC-002, DPP-BAT-008 · Source: [sec/DPP-SEC-002.yaml](sec/DPP-SEC-002.yaml)

### DPP-SEC-013

**Integrity proof is issued by the economic operator**

**SHOULD** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The integrity proof of a DPP SHOULD be issued with a key of the responsible economic operator or its authorised representative.

**Basis**

- prEN 18246:2025, 4.8.3 (draft standard)
- EN 18219:2026, 6.4.1 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The integrity proofs of the passport are verified (formats: `vc-data-integrity`, `vc-jose-cose` and `did-oyd-log`). Without a proof the result is skipped. At least one verified proof must be issued with a key of the DID at `$.economicOperatorId`; otherwise a warning.

**Notes** prEN 18246:2025 4.8.3 names the economic operator placing the product on the market, or its authorised representative, as the signer of core passport data; EN 18219:2026 6.4.1 describes economic operator DIDs as the means to sign passports, with the public key in the DID document. Passed if at least one proof verified under DPP-SEC-002 is issued with a key of the DID in economicOperatorId. A proof by another key gives a warning, because an authorised representative cannot be recognised automatically. For did-oyd-log the content is attested with the key of the passport identifier, which is not linked to the economic operator, so it gives a warning. Without a verified proof, or if economicOperatorId is not a DID, the result is skipped. Basis is a draft standard; the level follows its "should".

Catalogue rows: DPP-SEC-004 · Source: [sec/DPP-SEC-013.yaml](sec/DPP-SEC-013.yaml)

## Interoperability and standards

### DPP-INT-005

**Passport body follows the EN 18223 data model**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> The data elements of a DPP MUST follow the semantic model and the serialization of EN 18223.

**Basis**

- EN 18223:2026, 4.1.2.3–4.1.2.9, 5.2 (harmonised standard)

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure [`DigitalProductPassport`](../soya/DigitalProductPassport.yml); only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** Covers the DataElement classes (objectType), the attributes of Tables 2 to 6 and the value types of Table 7 in the expanded full serialization (Annex A). Whether an elementId is unique at its level is not checked: SOyA validates with SHACL Core, which cannot compare sibling nodes. Passports in the compressed serialization (5.2.5 to 5.2.9) are skipped until a structure for that form exists. Header attributes are checked by DPP-DAT-014.

## Product-specific: batteries

### DPP-BAT-002

**Battery passport exposes the public Annex XIII data**

**MUST** · checked on: published passport · automated · status: proposed · version 1

> A battery passport MUST make the information that Annex XIII lists as public accessible to everyone.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (Batteries)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1542/oj), Art. 77; Annex XIII (1) (regulation)

**Applies only if** the passport meets: `$.contentSpecificationIds[?search(@, '[Bb]atter')]` exists (otherwise skipped).

**How it is checked** The passport fetched via the product identifier is validated against the SHACL shapes of the SOyA structure `DigitalProductPassportBattery`; only the results tagged with this criterion's ID count.

**Notes** The SOyA structure DigitalProductPassportBattery takes its shapes from the OpenEPCIS validator resources (Apache 2.0). The rule that recognises a battery passport is fixed together with the linter.
